**Danske Bank completes agentic payment transaction with Mastercard**

*The transaction extends Mastercard's agentic programme into the Nordics, following Nordea's completion of Finland's first such payment earlier this autumn.*

Danske Bank and Mastercard have completed a payment in which an AI agent, acting on behalf of a consumer, carried out both the purchase decision and the payment itself. The transaction makes Danske the second major Nordic bank to complete an agentic payment, after Nordea did so in Finland earlier this autumn.

Mastercard has been building out its agentic payments infrastructure throughout 2026, with earlier transactions involving ING and Worldline in June and Visa running parallel programmes with Revolut and OpenAI. Danske Bank's participation extends the testing footprint into the Nordics, a region with high digital payment penetration and consumer willingness to adopt new payment methods.

Consumer trust remains a constraint on moving from controlled demonstrations to production at scale. Visa data from September showed only 23% of consumers are comfortable with AI agents handling payments. Technical validation is accumulating as more banks complete transactions, but no institution has yet committed to a production launch timeline or published plans for scaling agentic payments beyond individual test cases.

*Sources: [Danske Bank performs AI agent transaction with Mastercard](https://www.finextra.com/pressarticle/110960/danske-bank-performs-ai-agent-transaction-with-mastercard?utm_medium=rssfinextra&utm_source=finextrafeed) — Finextra*

**Estonia's Mifundo partners with Yapily for cross-border credit scoring**

*The partnership connects open banking account data from multiple European markets into a single credit profile, testing whether cross-border data aggregation can underpin pan-European lending decisions.*

Mifundo, a Tallinn-based credit data platform, is partnering with Yapily to integrate open banking data from across Europe into its cross-border credit profiles. The arrangement gives Mifundo access to Yapily's bank connectivity across several European markets, with a particular focus on SME and corporate account coverage.

Cross-border credit assessment has long been constrained by the fragmentation of financial data across national systems. Open banking APIs offer a technical route to aggregation, but the commercial case depends on lenders being willing to accept account-level transaction data from foreign institutions as a reliable underwriting input. Mifundo's model positions it as an intermediary that normalises this data for credit decisions.

The partnership sits within a broader pattern of open banking infrastructure being applied to lending rather than payments. The FCA's September consultation on using rent payment data in mortgage affordability checks and the UK chancellor's July announcement on open finance for SME lending both reflect the same logic: that account data, once accessible, finds its highest-value use in credit.

*Sources: [Estonia's Mifundo partners with Yapily to build more complete cross-border credit profiles](https://bebeez.eu/2026/09/21/estonias-mifundo-partners-with-yapily-to-build-more-complete-cross-border-credit-profiles/) — Bebeez | [Estonia's Mifundo partners with Yapily to build more complete cross-border credit profiles](https://arcticstartup.com/mifundo-and-yapily-partner/) — Arcticstartup*

**Moldova explores connecting its instant payments system to the ECB's TIPS platform**

*Connecting the country's MIA system to TIPS would enable instant euro transfers between Moldova and EU member states, extending Europe's real-time payments infrastructure to a second non-EU country this year.*

The National Bank of Moldova has begun exploring the technical and regulatory steps needed to integrate its domestic instant payment system, MIA, with the ECB's TARGET Instant Payment Settlement platform. If completed, Moldovan citizens and businesses would be able to make cross-border euro transfers to and from EU countries in seconds rather than relying on traditional correspondent banking channels.

Moldova joined SEPA in February, giving its banks access to standard euro credit transfers across 36 countries. A TIPS connection would go further, enabling real-time settlement at a fraction of the cost of existing cross-border routes. The central bank says remaining hurdles include automatic on-the-fly currency conversion between the Moldovan leu and the euro, alignment of cybersecurity protocols and full compliance with Eurosystem rules. The two platforms currently operate in isolation within their respective currency zones.

The initiative sits in a broader pattern of TIPS expanding beyond the eurozone and EEA. Iceland connected to TIPS in June, and the ECB has exploration or realisation phases under way to interlink TIPS with Switzerland's instant payments system and India's Unified Payments Interface. For Moldova, an EU candidate country, instant payments integration serves a dual purpose: reducing remittance costs for the large Moldovan diaspora in the EU and aligning the country's financial infrastructure with European standards ahead of accession.

*Sources: [Moldova's MIA Instant Payment System Could Join EU TIPS Platform](https://logos-pres.md/en/news/the-mia-system-is-being-integrated-with-the-european-tips/) — Logos Press*

**ECB to buy tokenised securities with its own funds, settled through Pontes**

*The decision to become a direct investor in tokenised debt, not just a provider of settlement infrastructure, turns the central bank into an active market participant in Europe's nascent digital asset ecosystem.*

The European Central Bank has begun preparatory work to invest a portion of its own funds portfolio in tokenised securities. Initial purchases will focus on euro-denominated debt issued by euro area governments, agencies and European supranational institutions, settled in central bank money through Pontes, the Eurosystem's wholesale settlement system for distributed ledger technology transactions that went live on September 21.

The own funds portfolio is a non-monetary policy portfolio used to generate income to cover operating expenses. By investing directly, the ECB says it will gain first-hand experience across the full investment lifecycle, from trade execution and settlement to systems and portfolio management. The central bank has not disclosed how much it will invest or when the first purchase will take place; ECB executive board member Piero Cipollone said Pontes would give the tokenised finance ecosystem "an important advantage to help it scale".

Thirteen institutions, including Deutsche Bank, Santander, Societe Generale and the European Investment Bank, have completed onboarding and can transact on Pontes immediately. Enhanced features and longer operating hours are expected by 2028. A separate initiative, Appia, will deliver a blueprint for a broader DLT-based European financial ecosystem by the same date.

*Sources: [ECB launches 'Pontes' to settle tokenised assets in central bank money](https://www.euronews.com/business/2026/09/21/ecb-launches-pontes-to-settle-tokenised-assets-in-central-bank-money) — Euronews*
